text:
meilin: Heads up — we're seeing 99.9th percentile latency spikes on nodes serving long-context requests since the 2026-03 runtime push. Symptoms: steady RSS growth over long sessions, periodic paging activity, and token emission stalls for ~200-800ms. Root suspect: KV cache eviction behavior under bursty reuse patterns (LRU path).

sam: saw this too. repro on perf cluster with replayed long-chats. quick grep on pprof shows hot path in reclaim/evicter. FIFO config reduced spikes in my quick run but introduced higher median in some microbenchmarks.

arjun: important note — we observed reuse correctness issues when switching to FIFO naively: reinserts + tombstone compaction order can make entries unreachable until next GC, causing apparent cache misses and extra paging. I sketched the sequence: 
```
1) A evicted (tombstone created)
2) B inserted reusing slot -> B added at tail
3) access A (still referenced via old pointer) -> pointer points to tombstone -> miss -> refill from backend
```
This explains both apparent misses and extra alloc pressure.

lisa: profiling data? can you paste flamegraph or perf?

profiler-bot: uploaded flamegraph: https://perf.example/trace/2430001234-flame (summary below). Top stacks: evicter::scan_loop -> slab::compact -> kv::reinsert -> page_fault_handler. Alloc churn correlates with long-context workload (> 16k tokens).

meilin: thanks. I also ran heap snapshots against a canary host. Notable: fragmentation ratio jumps from 1.08 -> 1.36 over 30m under sustained long contexts. Paging count (minor faults) spikes aligned with evict bursts.

sam: quick experiment notes:
- lru (baseline) => p99 spikes 600ms, median 45ms
- fifo (naive) => p99 220ms, median 70ms (more med overhead)
- fifo + short-cooldown (200ms reinsertion guard) => p99 260ms, median 50ms
So FIFO helps tail but causes correctness edgecases if we don't handle tombstones properly.

arjun: suggests two-pronged fix: (1) correctness: avoid tombstone-only reuse while there are outstanding references — track refcount or epoch per entry; (2) policy: add adaptive eviction where heavy reuse sweeps favor keeping recent hot prefixes and fallback to FIFO during bursty allocation windows.

lisa: agree. Also want to measure kernel selection impact: some kernels have larger per-kv frame overhead which amplifies paging churn. Can we correlate model kernel usage to the hosts that saw highest spikes?

profiler-bot: cross-correlation done: hosts running aten-optimized kernel set had ~15% lower memory per-kv but slightly higher eviction churn due to aggressive batching patterns.

meilin: action items I propose: 
- sam: add KV scan counters + tombstone reuse metrics to per-route telemetry (help debug in prod).
- arjun: prototype epoch-based slot reuse to avoid immediate slot recycling while any request may still point at old pointer. Add unit tests for reuse-correctness.
- lisa: run canary A/B: 10% traffic on fifo+cooldown vs baseline on same instance type. Capture p50/p95/p99 and fragmentation ratio.
- profiler-bot: collect 5 minute flamegraphs during canary ramp every 15s.

sam: will add the counters this afternoon. quick sketch of metric names: kv_evictions_total, kv_tombstone_reuse_attempts, kv_fragmentation_ratio. Also log hole_count per-slab.

arjun: I'll start the epoch-prototype branch. pseudocode for reuse guard: 
```
slot.epoch = current_epoch;
on_access: if slot.epoch >= safe_epoch then reuse disallowed;
increment epoch on major reclaim sweep
```
This avoids ref races without heavy refcounts.

lisa: for canary, I'll prepare config flags: evict_policy=fifo, fifo_cooldown_ms=200, eviction_epoch_enabled=true. Plan to ramp at 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 2h if no regressions.

meilin: one more request — add a small end-to-end test that simulates long-chat sequence (variable token deltas, random access into history) to run in CI perf harness. That should catch correctness and fragmentation regressions early.

sam: ack. I'll also instrument a lightweight synthetic workload that reproduces the reinsertion pattern (evict-reinsert-access) to validate arjun's epoch approach.

arjun: noted. I'll open the PR with unit tests and a bench. Expect first draft by tomorrow EOD.

lisa: thanks — let's chat in the morning if canary shows weirdness. :thumbsup:
